# Jany-Enesai Whitepaper Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Turn the Jany-Enesai proposal (`docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md`, draft 0.3) into a whitepaper whose every rune spelling and every treebank figure is regenerated by the engine and checked by a script, with the findings of the engine work written in, and record where the work stands so nothing done so far is lost.

**Architecture:** Two MIT scripts in `packages/engine/scripts/` follow the pattern of `check-whitepaper.ts`: `check-jany-enesai.ts` regenerates every rune spelling the proposal prints and runs in `npm test`. `rune-metrics.ts` recomputes the proposal's treebank figures from UD Kyrgyz-KTMU r2.18, fetched into a git-ignored `data/` directory, and fails when the document states a figure differently. The proposal is then edited until both pass, given a regenerated specimen figure and a description of the testbed, and linked from the Jany-Latyn whitepaper.

**Tech Stack:** TypeScript (engine, Node test runner, zero dependencies), Markdown, headless Google Chrome for one PNG.

**Spec:** `docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md` (draft 0.3, the document being finished) and `docs/jany-enesai/RUNES-SPEC.md` (§11 Conformance, §12 Revisions). The roadmap this comes from is a local plan file outside the repository. Its Phase 7, "Standalone whitepaper", reads: *"Write the Jany-Enesai whitepaper from draft 0.3: the alphabet, the settings, the reader/detector, the corpus and the congruity findings, and any glyph revisions from Phase 4. Add a conformance checker like `scripts/check-whitepaper.ts`, so every runic example in the paper is generated and verified. Add a pointer from the Jany-Latyn `WHITEPAPER.md` §7 and its Appendix D."*

### Decisions already taken

- **2026-10-15, R1–R5 and Q1** (`RUNES-SPEC.md` §12): Eski-Enesai, the stones' majority forms, is the inscription look shown first, and the Orkhon look is kept as a reference. нт is 𐰦 in every inscription look. р, с, ш can each take the stones' form (𐰻 𐰾 𐱀). One sentence covers 𐱈 = *baš*. Proposal §21.1 reports the corpus. Eski-Enesai keeps ш 𐱀 apart from back с 𐱂, with a merge toggle.
- **The author's concern about ш** (a stroke on the fork of front л 𐰠, close to 𐰱) is recorded as the first design input for the experimental scheme (`RUNES-SPEC.md` §3.1), not as a change to the reference schemes.
- **2026-10-15, legibility review:** none of the 28 runes changes. New toggles: ж as 𐰙, and per-letter attested р/с/ш, with с and ш marked "hard to read". The bundled font should exaggerate the strokes that separate ы/и, ө/ү, ч/ж (`RUNES-SPEC.md` §4.7). Added `glyph-legibility.png`, and a note that х 𐰝 is the syllable *ök* on the stones (§8).
- **The author's guidance on р, с, ш:** favour readers of modern Kyrgyz over Turkish- or Russian-leaning conventions. The sources in circulation known so far are the video chart and the rune titles of the Teñir-uulu YouTube channel (about 15k subscribers). The survey of charts (§27.4) settles the reference.
- **2026-10-16, the qylym site:** Playground · Latin ▾ · Runic ▾ · About; any-to-any conversion; the proposal published as a page marked "Draft for review"; new interface strings in English only; rune votes and events treated like the Latin ones.

### What the engine and the treebank show (measured for this plan)

The figures were re-run with the engine over UD Kyrgyz-KTMU r2.18 (commit `7427f47f8d5b44156cc2a657bf6e3c8f002693f9`). The prototype's counts are reproduced exactly when a word is a run of Cyrillic letters in each sentence's `# text =` line, with hyphenated parts joined, and types are lowercased.

Other findings:
- **Jany-Latyn questions (not decided here).** Four reverse-conversion behaviours belong to Jany-Latyn, not the runes. Three are rules that lose Kyrgyz spellings: iotated е after a vowel, `i` after a vowel read as й (a rule kept for older text that wrote the glide as plain `i`), and `sh` read as ш where it is с + х. The fourth is the loan list putting ь into Kyrgyz case forms. The runes' round trip equals Jany-Latyn's own on every token. Changing Jany-Latyn is the author's decision; Task 4 reports these questions in the proposal (§27.7) and changes no engine code.
- **The checker against draft 0.3:** 466 of 467 checks pass. The one failure is the heading "Jany-Enesaí" in Appendix B (Appendix A uses the same spelling in its column header and cells). The rest of the document uses the plain form "Jany-Enesai" (§1: *Jany-Enesai* is the plain form of *Jaŋy Enesaí*).
- **Font download:** the Noto repository has no hinted WOFF2 for Old Turkic (404). The hinted TTF (15 KB) is at `…/NotoSansOldTurkic/hinted/ttf/NotoSansOldTurkic-Regular.ttf`. The playground plan's Task 4 was corrected to use it.
- **The specimen:** `orhon-enesai-specimen.png` (§4) shows the draft 0.2 settings and lacks Eski-Enesai and Attested letters. Headless Chrome renders a correct replacement from an HTML page in the bundled font.
- **Stale status lines:** the proposal and `RUNES-SPEC.md` still say "Not implemented" / "Nothing here is implemented in the engine yet".
- **Reference gap:** §13.1 cites the Apertium Kyrgyz lexicon, but the reference list has no entry for it. Its counts (24 stems with a vowel + е, 2 with a vowel + йе) were not re-run.

### Decisions this plan makes (change them before executing if you disagree)

1. **The whitepaper is `docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md`, finished in place,** not a new `WHITEPAPER.md`. `RUNES-SPEC.md`, the corpus, the engine's tests and comments, the golden fixture, and the playground's `/runic/proposal/` route all cite it by name and section. A second file would drift from it.
2. **Section numbers do not change.** New material goes into new subsections (§14.1, §27.7), table rows, and sentences.
3. **The version becomes draft 0.4.** Naming a release (1.0, or a calendar version with the repository) is left to the release, outside this plan.
4. **Jany-Latyn's questions are reported, not answered.** No engine code changes in this plan, and `npm test` keeps the whitepaper check at 208/208.
5. **The treebank is pinned to UD r2.18,** commit `7427f47f8d5b44156cc2a657bf6e3c8f002693f9`.

## Global Constraints

- Engine scripts and tests are MIT and start with `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`. They import only engine siblings and `node:` built-ins (`test/boundary.test.ts`). Reading `docs/` or `data/` files at run time is allowed, as `check-whitepaper.ts` does.
- The UD treebank is CC BY-SA 4.0. It lives only in `data/` (git-ignored) and is never committed; no text from it goes into a fixture or a test. Nothing from `corpus/` (CC BY-NC-SA) goes into the engine or its tests.
- No existing Jany-Latyn output changes; `npm test` keeps `Whitepaper check (docs/WHITEPAPER.md): 208/208 passed`.
- No `toUpperCase`/`toLowerCase` in engine code; use `lowerStr` from `casing.ts`.
- Rune text is handled by code point, with the `u` flag on every regular expression that can see runes.
- Relative imports in the engine end in `.js`.
- Docs are CC BY 4.0. They follow the proposal's own style: plain, measured sentences; a claim is paired with the test that would settle it; figures appear exactly as `rune-metrics` prints them (en-US thousands separators, percentages with one decimal unless the document's table uses whole numbers).
- Verification (AGENTS.md): `npm test`, `npm run chart`, `npm run check:web`, `npm run build:web`, plus `npm run test:corpus` and `npm run rune-metrics -- --check`.

## Review Focus

1. **A fresh clone, or CI, without the treebank:** `npm test` must pass without `data/`, and `npm run rune-metrics` must exit 2 with the fetch command. Pinned by the "without the treebank" test in Task 2.
2. **A figure reworded or reformatted in the document** ("96.3 %", or a line break inside the sentence): `--check` must report it rather than pass. Pinned by the "one wrong figure is reported" test in Task 2.
3. **A new setting column or row added to a comparison table:** the checker must fail until the label is mapped, rather than skip the column. Pinned by the "unknown setting column" test in Task 3.
4. **A different treebank release in `data/`** (someone clones `dev` or r2.19): the figures would silently change. Pinned by the commit check in `fetch-ud-kyrgyz.sh` (Task 1, Step 5).
5. **The specimen rendered with a fallback font** (a wrong `--font` path): Chrome would still write a PNG, in the wrong glyphs. Pinned by the "font file that does not exist is refused" test in Task 5, and by viewing the PNG in Task 5, Step 4.

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `packages/engine/scripts/treebank.ts`**

```ts
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/**
 * Reads UD Kyrgyz-KTMU (CC BY-SA 4.0) for the figures of the Jany-Enesai proposal.
 * The treebank is read at run time from a git-ignored directory that
 * scripts/fetch-ud-kyrgyz.sh fills; nothing from it is committed.
 *
 * The proposal counts words the way its draft prototype did: runs of Cyrillic
 * letters in each sentence's `# text = ` line, with hyphenated parts joined
 * (Ысык-Көл is one word), and word types lowercased.
 */
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { lowerStr } from '../src/casing.js';

export const TREEBANK_FILES = ['ky_ktmu-ud-train.conllu', 'ky_ktmu-ud-test.conllu'] as const;

export const TREEBANK_WORD = /\p{Script=Cyrillic}+(?:-\p{Script=Cyrillic}+)*/gu;

export interface Treebank {
  /** Sentences in the files (`# sent_id` lines). Ten of r2.18's have no text line. */
  sentenceIds: number;
  /** The `# text = ` line of every sentence that has one. */
  texts: string[];
  /** Lowercased form → lemma and part of speech of its first occurrence as a syntactic word. */
  forms: Map<string, { lemma: string; upos: string }>;
}

export function parseConllu(sources: readonly string[]): Treebank {
  const tb: Treebank = { sentenceIds: 0, texts: [], forms: new Map() };
  for (const source of sources) {
    for (const line of source.split('\n')) {
      if (line.startsWith('# sent_id')) tb.sentenceIds++;
      else if (line.startsWith('# text = ')) tb.texts.push(line.slice('# text = '.length));
      else if (/^\d+\t/.test(line)) {
        const [, form, lemma, upos] = line.split('\t');
        const key = lowerStr(form);
        if (!tb.forms.has(key)) tb.forms.set(key, { lemma: lowerStr(lemma), upos });
      }
    }
  }
  return tb;
}

export function readTreebank(dir: string): Treebank {
  return parseConllu(TREEBANK_FILES.map((f) => readFileSync(join(dir, f), 'utf8')));
}

/** Every word token of the texts, lowercased, in order. */
export function treebankWords(texts: readonly string[]): string[] {
  return texts.flatMap((t) => t.match(TREEBANK_WORD) ?? []).map((w) => lowerStr(w));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 5: The fetch script and the ignore rule**

Create `packages/engine/scripts/fetch-ud-kyrgyz.sh` and make it executable (`chmod +x`):

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# Fetches UD Kyrgyz-KTMU (CC BY-SA 4.0), release r2.18, into data/ at the repository
# root, which git ignores. `npm run rune-metrics` computes the figures of
# docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md from it. Never commit it.
set -eu
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../.." && pwd)
DEST="$ROOT/data/UD_Kyrgyz-KTMU"
TAG=r2.18
COMMIT=7427f47f8d5b44156cc2a657bf6e3c8f002693f9
if [ ! -d "$DEST/.git" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$ROOT/data"
  git clone --quiet --depth 1 --branch "$TAG" https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Kyrgyz-KTMU "$DEST"
fi
# The figures are pinned to one release; another one would change them silently.
actual=$(git -C "$DEST" rev-parse HEAD)
if [ "$actual" != "$COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "data/UD_Kyrgyz-KTMU is at $actual, not $TAG ($COMMIT). Remove it and run this again." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "UD Kyrgyz-KTMU $TAG in $DEST"
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `packages/engine/scripts/rune-metrics.ts`**

```ts
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/**
 * The treebank figures of the Jany-Enesai proposal (docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md),
 * computed with the engine itself over UD Kyrgyz-KTMU r2.18.
 *
 * Run:   npm run rune-metrics                 (prints the figures)
 *        npm run rune-metrics -- --check      (fails if the proposal states a figure differently)
 *        npm run rune-metrics -- --json
 * Needs the treebank: packages/engine/scripts/fetch-ud-kyrgyz.sh
 */
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { cyrToJany, janyToCyr } from '../src/convert.js';
import { lowerStr } from '../src/casing.js';
import {
  cyrillicToRunes, janyLatynToRunes, runesToJanyLatyn, explainRunes, presetOptions, RUNE_PRESETS,
} from '../src/runes/index.js';
import { readTreebank, treebankWords, type Treebank } from './treebank.js';

const VOWELS = 'аэиоуыөүеёюя';

/** Why a token does not come back unchanged; a token counts under the first cause that applies (proposal §13.1). */
export const CAUSES: readonly { label: string; test: (w: string) => boolean }[] = [
  { label: '`ц`', test: (w) => w.includes('ц') },
  { label: 'Iotated `е` after a vowel', test: (w) => new RegExp(`[${VOWELS}]е`).test(w) },
  { label: '`ъ`, `ь`', test: (w) => /[ъь]/.test(w) },
  { label: '`э` after a consonant', test: (w) => new RegExp(`[^${VOWELS}-]э`).test(w) },
  { label: '`ё` against `йо`', test: (w) => /ё|йо/.test(w) },
  { label: '`э` after a vowel', test: (w) => new RegExp(`[${VOWELS}]э`).test(w) },
  { label: '`и` after a vowel', test: (w) => new RegExp(`[${VOWELS}]и`).test(w) },
  { label: '`с` before `х`', test: (w) => w.includes('сх') },
];

// The consonants with a back and a front rune (proposal §6), by their Jany-Latyn letter.
const PAIRED: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  b: 'б', g: 'г', d: 'д', j: 'ж', 'í': 'й', k: 'к', l: 'л', n: 'н', r: 'р', s: 'с', t: 'т',
};
const BACK_VOWELS = new Set([...'ayou']);

export interface Reverse {
  lostTokens: number;
  forms: number;
  lemmas: number;
  causes: Record<string, number>;
}

export interface RuneMetrics {
  corpus: { sentenceIds: number; sentences: number; tokens: number; types: number };
  /** Share of each paired consonant's occurrences governed by a back vowel, by Cyrillic letter. */
  backShare: Record<string, number>;
  backShareOverall: number;
  mixedVowelTypes: number;
  /** Sentences that come back from runes as the identical Jany-Latyn, per reversible preset. */
  roundTrip: Record<string, number>;
  /** Word types sharing a rune spelling with a type of another Jany-Latyn spelling. */
  sharedTypes: Record<string, number>;
  janyLatynShared: string[];
  letterTokens: Record<string, number>;
  roundedVowels: Record<string, number>;
  harmonyChanged: { kg: number; full: number };
  reverse: Reverse;
  reverseWithList: Reverse;
  postVocalicE: { tokens: number; forms: [string, string][] };
  vowelYeTokens: number;
  loanList: { fixed: string[]; broken: string[] };
  /** The runes each preset writes on the treebank, sorted by code point. */
  emitted: Record<string, string>;
  collation: { icu: string; equal: string[] };
}

const fraction = (n: number, d: number) => (d === 0 ? 0 : n / d);

export function computeMetrics(tb: Treebank): RuneMetrics {
  const words = treebankWords(tb.texts);
  const types = [...new Set(words)];
  const jl = new Map(types.map((t) => [t, lowerStr(cyrToJany(t))]));

  const back: Record<string, number> = {};
  const all: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const w of explainRunes(words.join(' '))) {
    for (const l of w.letters) {
      if (!(l.letter in PAIRED) || l.governor === null) continue;
      const c = PAIRED[l.letter];
      all[c] = (all[c] ?? 0) + 1;
      if (BACK_VOWELS.has(w.letters[l.governor].letter)) back[c] = (back[c] ?? 0) + 1;
    }
  }
  const sum = (o: Record<string, number>) => Object.values(o).reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);

  const roundTrip: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const p of RUNE_PRESETS.filter((p) => p.reversible)) {
    roundTrip[p.id] = tb.texts.filter((t) => {
      const j = lowerStr(cyrToJany(t));
      return runesToJanyLatyn(janyLatynToRunes(j, p.options)) === j;
    }).length;
  }

  const shared = (options: Parameters<typeof cyrillicToRunes>[1]) => {
    const byRunes = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
    const runesOf = new Map(types.map((t) => [t, cyrillicToRunes(t, options)]));
    for (const t of types) {
      const r = runesOf.get(t)!;
      if (!byRunes.has(r)) byRunes.set(r, new Set());
      byRunes.get(r)!.add(jl.get(t)!);
    }
    return types.filter((t) => byRunes.get(runesOf.get(t)!)!.size > 1).length;
  };
  const sharedTypes: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const p of RUNE_PRESETS) sharedTypes[p.id] = shared(p.options);
  sharedTypes['zhe-etymological'] = shared({ zhe: 'etymological' });

  const byJanyLatyn = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const t of types) byJanyLatyn.set(jl.get(t)!, [...(byJanyLatyn.get(jl.get(t)!) ?? []), t]);

  const reference = new Map(types.map((t) => [t, cyrillicToRunes(t)]));
  const changed = (id: string) =>
    fraction(types.filter((t) => cyrillicToRunes(t, presetOptions(id)) !== reference.get(t)).length, types.length);

  const back2cyr = (w: string, restoreLoans: boolean) =>
    lowerStr(janyToCyr(runesToJanyLatyn(cyrillicToRunes(w)), { restoreLoans }));
  const reverse = (restoreLoans: boolean): Reverse => {
    const lost = words.filter((w) => back2cyr(w, restoreLoans) !== w);
    const forms = new Set(lost);
    const causes: Record<string, number> = {};
    for (const w of lost) {
      const label = CAUSES.find((c) => c.test(w))?.label ?? 'other';
      causes[label] = (causes[label] ?? 0) + 1;
    }
    return {
      lostTokens: lost.length,
      forms: forms.size,
      lemmas: new Set([...forms].map((f) => tb.forms.get(f)?.lemma ?? f)).size,
      causes,
    };
  };

  const postVocalic = new RegExp(`[${VOWELS}]е`);
  const eLost = words.filter((w) => postVocalic.test(w) && back2cyr(w, false) !== w);

  const emitted: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const p of RUNE_PRESETS) {
    const runes = new Set([...cyrillicToRunes(words.join(' '), p.options)].filter((c) => /\p{Script=Old_Turkic}/u.test(c)));
    emitted[p.id] = [...runes].sort((a, b) => a.codePointAt(0)! - b.codePointAt(0)!).join('');
  }

  const letters = [...'абвгдежзийклмнңоөпрстуүфхчшы'].map((c) => [c, cyrillicToRunes(c)] as const);
  const collator = new Intl.Collator('und', { sensitivity: 'base' });
  const equal: string[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < letters.length; i++) {
    for (let j = i + 1; j < letters.length; j++) {
      if (letters[i][1] !== letters[j][1] && collator.compare(letters[i][1], letters[j][1]) === 0) {
        equal.push(`${letters[i][0]}=${letters[j][0]}`);
      }
    }
  }

  const rounded: Record<string, number> = { о: 0, у: 0, ө: 0, ү: 0 };
  for (const w of words) for (const ch of w) if (ch in rounded) rounded[ch]++;

  return {
    corpus: { sentenceIds: tb.sentenceIds, sentences: tb.texts.length, tokens: words.length, types: types.length },
    backShare: Object.fromEntries(Object.values(PAIRED).map((c) => [c, fraction(back[c] ?? 0, all[c] ?? 0)])),
    backShareOverall: fraction(sum(back), sum(all)),
    mixedVowelTypes: fraction(types.filter((t) => /[ayou]/.test(jl.get(t)!) && /[eiöü]/.test(jl.get(t)!)).length, types.length),
    roundTrip,
    sharedTypes,
    janyLatynShared: [...byJanyLatyn.values()].filter((v) => v.length > 1).map((v) => v.join('/')),
    letterTokens: Object.fromEntries(['ж', 'в', 'ф', 'х'].map((c) => [c, fraction(words.filter((w) => w.includes(c)).length, words.length)])),
    roundedVowels: rounded,
    harmonyChanged: { kg: changed('kg'), full: changed('full') },
    reverse: reverse(false),
    reverseWithList: reverse(true),
    postVocalicE: {
      tokens: eLost.length,
      forms: [...new Set(eLost)].map((f) => [f, tb.forms.get(f)?.upos ?? '?'] as [string, string]),
    },
    vowelYeTokens: words.filter((w) => new RegExp(`[${VOWELS}]йе`).test(w)).length,
    loanList: {
      fixed: [...new Set(words.filter((w) => back2cyr(w, false) !== w && back2cyr(w, true) === w))],
      broken: [...new Set(words.filter((w) => back2cyr(w, false) === w && back2cyr(w, true) !== w))],
    },
    emitted,
    collation: { icu: process.versions.icu ?? 'none', equal },
  };
}

const num = (n: number) => n.toLocaleString('en-US');
const pct = (f: number, digits = 1) => `${(100 * f).toFixed(digits)}%`;

/** Each figure exactly as the proposal must state it (proposal draft 0.4). */
export function figures(m: RuneMetrics): { section: string; text: string }[] {
  const r = m.reverse;
  const unchanged = fraction(m.corpus.tokens - r.lostTokens, m.corpus.tokens);
  const share = Object.values(m.backShare).map((f) => pct(f, 0));
  const lo = Math.min(...Object.values(m.backShare));
  const hi = Math.max(...Object.values(m.backShare));
  const at = (f: number) => Object.entries(m.backShare).filter(([, v]) => pct(v, 0) === pct(f, 0)).map(([c]) => c).join(', ');
  return [
    { section: 'Abstract', text: `On a Kyrgyz treebank, ${pct(unchanged)} of word tokens come back unchanged` },
    { section: '§5.3', text: `${num(m.corpus.sentences)} sentences of news and fiction, ${num(m.corpus.tokens)} Cyrillic word tokens, and ${num(m.corpus.types)} word types` },
    { section: '§6', text: `between ${pct(lo, 0)} (${at(lo)}) and ${pct(hi, 0)} (${at(hi)})` },
    { section: '§6', text: `| In back-vowel syllables | ${share.join(' | ')} |` },
    { section: '§7.3', text: `all ${num(m.corpus.sentences)} treebank sentences convert to runes and back to the identical Jany-Latyn` },
    { section: '§8', text: `ж occurs in ${pct(m.letterTokens['ж'])} of word tokens, в in ${pct(m.letterTokens['в'])}, ф in ${pct(m.letterTokens['ф'])}, and х in ${pct(m.letterTokens['х'])}` },
    { section: '§13.1', text: `${pct(unchanged)} of the treebank's ${num(m.corpus.tokens)} word tokens come back unchanged` },
    { section: '§13.1', text: `${num(r.forms)} distinct word forms of ${num(r.lemmas)} lemmas` },
    ...CAUSES.map((c) => ({ section: '§13.1', text: `| ${c.label} | ${num(r.causes[c.label] ?? 0)} |` })),
    { section: '§13.1', text: `every one of the ${num(m.postVocalicE.tokens)} tokens that spell plain \`е\`` },
    { section: '§13.2', text: `about ${num(Math.round(r.lemmas / 10) * 10)} lemmas` },
    { section: '§13.2', text: `the list restores ${num(m.loanList.fixed.length)} word forms and spoils ${num(m.loanList.broken.length)}` },
    { section: '§14', text: `it changes ${pct(m.harmonyChanged.kg)} of the treebank's word types. Full harmony changes ${pct(m.harmonyChanged.full)}` },
    { section: '§17', text: `${num(m.sharedTypes['orkhon'])} word types (${pct(fraction(m.sharedTypes['orkhon'], m.corpus.types))})` },
    { section: '§17', text: `${num(m.sharedTypes['eski-enesai'])} word types (${pct(fraction(m.sharedTypes['eski-enesai'], m.corpus.types))})` },
    { section: '§15', text: `the ${pct(m.mixedVowelTypes, 0)} of word types in the treebank that contain both back and front vowels` },
  ];
}

/** Claims the proposal makes in words rather than figures; each must hold. */
export function claims(m: RuneMetrics): { section: string; claim: string; holds: boolean }[] {
  const max = Math.max(...Object.values(m.roundedVowels));
  return [
    { section: '§7.3', claim: 'every reversible preset round-trips every sentence', holds: Object.values(m.roundTrip).every((n) => n === m.corpus.sentences) },
    { section: '§14', claim: 'no shared rune spelling beyond Jany-Latyn in Jany-Enesai, k+g, full harmony, attested letters', holds: ['jany-enesai', 'kg', 'full', 'attested'].every((id) => m.sharedTypes[id] === 0) },
    { section: '§18', claim: 'the etymological ж creates no shared spelling', holds: m.sharedTypes['zhe-etymological'] === 0 },
    { section: '§13.1', claim: 'no word spells й + е after a vowel', holds: m.vowelYeTokens === 0 },
    { section: '§13.1', claim: 'every lost token falls under a cause in the table', holds: !m.reverse.causes['other'] },
    { section: '§27.3', claim: 'у is the commonest rounded vowel', holds: m.roundedVowels['у'] === max },
    { section: '§8', claim: 'exactly и/ы, ү/ө, ж/ч, ф/л, в/б compare equal at base strength', holds: [...m.collation.equal].sort().join(' ') === 'б=в ж=ч и=ы л=ф ө=ү' },
  ];
}

const APPENDIX_A_LABELS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  'J-E': 'jany-enesai', 'k+g': 'kg', Full: 'full', Orkh: 'orkhon', Eski: 'eski-enesai', Att: 'attested',
};

/** The runes Appendix A's "Emitted by" column gives each preset, sorted by code point. */
export function appendixAEmitted(doc: string): Record<string, string> {
  const out: Record<string, string[]> = Object.fromEntries(Object.values(APPENDIX_A_LABELS).map((id) => [id, []]));
  const appendix = doc.slice(doc.indexOf('## Appendix A.'), doc.indexOf('## Appendix B.'));
  for (const line of appendix.split('\n')) {
    const cells = line.split('|').map((c) => c.trim());
    if (!/^U\+10C[0-4][0-9A-F]$/.test(cells[1] ?? '')) continue;
    for (const label of cells[6].split(',').map((s) => s.trim())) {
      if (label in APPENDIX_A_LABELS) out[APPENDIX_A_LABELS[label]].push(cells[2]);
    }
  }
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(out).map(([id, rs]) => [id, rs.sort((a, b) => a.codePointAt(0)! - b.codePointAt(0)!).join('')]));
}

/** Everything in the proposal that disagrees with the metrics; empty when it agrees. */
export function checkDocument(doc: string, m: RuneMetrics): string[] {
  const problems = figures(m).filter((f) => !doc.includes(f.text)).map((f) => `${f.section}: the document should say "${f.text}"`);
  problems.push(...claims(m).filter((c) => !c.holds).map((c) => `${c.section}: the claim "${c.claim}" does not hold`));
  const stated = appendixAEmitted(doc);
  for (const [id, runes] of Object.entries(m.emitted)) {
    if (stated[id] !== runes) problems.push(`Appendix A: "Emitted by" for ${id} lists ${stated[id]}, the engine writes ${runes}`);
  }
  return problems;
}

export function formatMetrics(m: RuneMetrics): string {
  const rows = [
    ...figures(m).map((f) => `| ${f.section} | ${f.text.replace(/\|/g, '\\|')} |`),
    ...claims(m).map((c) => `| ${c.section} | ${c.holds ? 'holds' : 'DOES NOT HOLD'}: ${c.claim} |`),
    `| §7.3 | words sharing a Jany-Latyn spelling: ${m.janyLatynShared.join(', ')} |`,
    `| §13.1 | other lost tokens: ${m.reverse.causes['other'] ?? 0}; with the loan list: ${m.reverseWithList.lostTokens} lost |`,
    `| §13.1 | post-vocalic е forms (UPOS): ${m.postVocalicE.forms.map(([f, u]) => `${f} (${u})`).join(', ')} |`,
    `| §13.2 | the loan list restores: ${m.loanList.fixed.join(', ')}; spoils: ${m.loanList.broken.join(', ')} |`,
    `| §8 | collation: ICU ${m.collation.icu}, equal at base strength: ${m.collation.equal.join(' ')} |`,
  ];
  return ['| Section | Figure |', '| :--- | :--- |', ...rows].join('\n');
}

function main(argv: string[]): number {
  const dirArg = argv.indexOf('--dir');
  const dir = dirArg >= 0 ? argv[dirArg + 1] : fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../data/UD_Kyrgyz-KTMU/', import.meta.url));
  let tb: Treebank;
  try {
    tb = readTreebank(dir);
  } catch {
    process.stderr.write(`UD Kyrgyz-KTMU not found in ${dir}; run packages/engine/scripts/fetch-ud-kyrgyz.sh\n`);
    return 2;
  }
  const m = computeMetrics(tb);
  if (argv.includes('--json')) {
    process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(m, null, 1) + '\n');
    return 0;
  }
  process.stdout.write(formatMetrics(m) + '\n');
  if (!argv.includes('--check')) return 0;
  const docArg = argv.indexOf('--doc');
  const doc = readFileSync(docArg >= 0 ? argv[docArg + 1] : new URL('../../../../docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md', import.meta.url), 'utf8');
  const problems = checkDocument(doc, m);
  for (const p of problems) process.stderr.write(`✗ ${p}\n`);
  process.stdout.write(`Proposal figures: ${problems.length === 0 ? 'all agree' : `${problems.length} disagree`}\n`);
  return problems.length === 0 ? 0 : 1;
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) process.exit(main(process.argv.slice(2)));
```

### Task 3: `check-jany-enesai`, every rune spelling in the proposal

**Files:**
- Create: `packages/engine/scripts/check-jany-enesai.ts`
- Modify: `packages/engine/package.json` (`test`, new `check-jany-enesai`), `package.json`, `docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md` (two label fixes and one sentence)
- Test: `packages/engine/test/checkJanyEnesai.test.ts` (create)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `cyrToJany`; from `../src/runes/index.js`: `cyrillicToRunes`, `janyLatynToRunes`, `presetOptions`, `isReversible`, `runeName`, `RuneOptions`.
- Produces:
  - `SETTING_LABELS: Record<string, string>`, mapping a table label to a preset id.
  - `EXAMPLES`: the hand-kept prose examples.
  - `interface Report { passed: number; failures: string[] }`
  - `checkDocument(doc: string): Report`
  - CLI: `npm run check-jany-enesai`, also run at the end of `npm test`. It prints `Jany-Enesai check (docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md): N/N passed`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```ts
// packages/engine/test/checkJanyEnesai.test.ts
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/**
 * The proposal checker (scripts/check-jany-enesai.ts) on small documents: it
 * passes what the engine writes, reports what it does not, and fails on a
 * comparison column it does not know.
 */
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { checkDocument } from '../scripts/check-jany-enesai.js';

const PASSAGE = [
  '> **Cyrillic.** Кол.', '>', '> **Jany-Latyn.** Kol.', '>', '> **Jany-Enesai** (read right to left):', '>', '> 𐰴𐰆𐰞.',
].join('\n');
// EXAMPLES must still find their runes in the document.
const EXAMPLE_RUNES = '𐰳𐰀𐰭𐰃 𐰅𐰣𐰅𐰽𐰀𐰖 𐰴𐰆𐰽𐰢𐰆𐰽 𐱅𐰅𐰢𐰄𐰼𐰳𐰆𐰞 𐰴𐰃𐰻𐰎𐰕 𐰶𐰃𐰺𐰍𐰔 𐱅𐰭𐰼 𐰜𐰇𐰠';

const doc = (body: string) => ['## 4. In Running Text', PASSAGE, '', '## 5. Body', body, '', EXAMPLE_RUNES].join('\n');

test('check-jany-enesai: tables, names, and examples the engine writes pass', () => {
  const report = checkDocument(doc([
    '| Cyrillic | Jany-Latyn | Jany-Enesai | Full harmony | Eski-Enesai |',
    '| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |',
    '| кол | kol | 𐰴𐰆𐰞 | 𐰸𐰆𐰞 | 𐰹𐰆𐰞 |',
    '',
    '| Rune | Unicode name |',
    '| :---: | :--- |',
    '| 𐰴 | ORKHON AQ |',
    '',
    'Long vowels are doubled: *тоо* (mountain) 𐱄𐰆𐰆.',
  ].join('\n')));
  assert.deepEqual(report.failures, []);
  assert.ok(report.passed >= 8, String(report.passed));
});

test('check-jany-enesai: a wrong rune, name, or example is reported where it is', () => {
  const report = checkDocument(doc([
    '| Cyrillic | Jany-Enesai |',
    '| :--- | :--- |',
    '| кол | 𐰸𐰆𐰞 |',
    '',
    '| Rune | Unicode name |',
    '| :---: | :--- |',
    '| 𐰴 | ORKHON AK |',
    '',
    'And *туу* 𐱄𐰆𐰆.',
  ].join('\n')));
  assert.equal(report.failures.length, 3);
  assert.ok(report.failures.every((f) => f.startsWith('§5:')), report.failures.join('\n'));
});

test('check-jany-enesai: an unknown setting column fails instead of going unchecked', () => {
  const report = checkDocument(doc([
    '| Cyrillic | Jany-Enesai | Jany-Enesaí |',
    '| :--- | :--- | :--- |',
    '| кол | 𐰴𐰆𐰞 | 𐰴𐰆𐰞 |',
  ].join('\n')));
  assert.deepEqual(report.failures, ['§5: comparison column "Jany-Enesaí" is not a known setting (add it to SETTING_LABELS or NOTE_COLUMNS)']);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `packages/engine/scripts/check-jany-enesai.ts`**

```ts
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/**
 * Conformance checker for the Jany-Enesai proposal (docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md),
 * the counterpart of check-whitepaper.ts. Every rune spelling the proposal prints
 * is regenerated by the engine:
 *
 *  - comparison tables: a first column of Cyrillic and one column per setting
 *    (§14 settings ladder, §16 chart title, Appendix B);
 *  - the alphabet table of §2 (Jany-Latyn letter → rune);
 *  - every "Rune | Unicode name" pair in any table (§2, §8, §14, Appendix A, which
 *    also states the code point);
 *  - the §4 passage;
 *  - word examples in prose and tables: an italic Cyrillic word followed by its
 *    runes (*кол* 𐰴𐰆𐰞), read in Jany-Enesai unless EXAMPLE_SETTINGS says otherwise;
 *  - EXAMPLES, a hand-kept list for examples the patterns cannot reach.
 *
 * A comparison-table column whose label is not a known setting fails the run, so
 * a new column cannot go unchecked.
 *
 * Run: npm run check-jany-enesai   (also part of npm test)
 */
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { cyrToJany } from '../src/convert.js';
import {
  cyrillicToRunes, janyLatynToRunes, presetOptions, isReversible, runeName, type RuneOptions,
} from '../src/runes/index.js';

// Column and row labels of the comparison tables, and the setting each names.
// "The chart's rune line" is §16's quotation of the chart, which full harmony reproduces exactly.
export const SETTING_LABELS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  'Jany-Enesai': 'jany-enesai',
  'k+g harmony': 'kg',
  'Full harmony': 'full',
  'Eski-Enesai': 'eski-enesai',
  'Inscription look (Orkhon forms)': 'orkhon',
  'Attested letters': 'attested',
  Lossless: 'jany-enesai',
  "The chart's rune line": 'full',
};
// Columns of comparison tables that hold no rune spelling.
const NOTE_COLUMNS = new Set(['Jany-Latyn', 'Changes from Jany-Enesai', 'Reversible?', 'Needs a word list?']);
const SOURCE_COLUMNS = new Set(['Cyrillic', 'Title word']);

// Prose word examples that are not in Jany-Enesai, by "word → runes".
const EXAMPLE_SETTINGS: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {};

interface Example { where: string; source: string; runes: string; options?: Partial<RuneOptions>; from?: 'jany-latyn' }

// Examples the patterns cannot reach: prose that names the setting in words.
export const EXAMPLES: readonly Example[] = [
  { where: 'Part I', source: 'jaŋy enesaí', runes: '𐰳𐰀𐰭𐰃 𐰅𐰣𐰅𐰽𐰀𐰖', from: 'jany-latyn' },
  { where: '§15', source: 'космос', runes: '𐰴𐰆𐰽𐰢𐰆𐰽', options: presetOptions('kg') },
  { where: '§15', source: 'Темиржол', runes: '𐱅𐰅𐰢𐰄𐰼𐰳𐰆𐰞', options: presetOptions('full') },
  { where: '§17', source: 'кыргыз', runes: '𐰴𐰃𐰻𐰎𐰕', options: presetOptions('eski-enesai') },
  { where: '§17', source: 'кыргыз', runes: '𐰶𐰃𐰺𐰍𐰔', options: presetOptions('orkhon') },
  { where: '§17', source: 'Теңир', runes: '𐱅𐰭𐰼', options: presetOptions('orkhon') },
  { where: '§6', source: 'көл', runes: '𐰜𐰇𐰠', options: presetOptions('full') },
];

export interface Report { passed: number; failures: string[] }

// The tables print every setting with spaces between words, as Appendix B says;
// the inscription looks themselves put the two-dot divider there.
const inTables = (id: string): RuneOptions => ({ ...presetOptions(id), separator: 'space' });

const RUNE_RUN = /[\p{Script=Old_Turkic}̇\u{10CEA}]+(?:[ -][\p{Script=Old_Turkic}̇\u{10CEA}]+)*/u;
const strip = (s: string) => s.replace(/\*\*|\*|`/g, '').trim();
const cellsOf = (line: string) => line.trim().split('|').slice(1, -1).map((c) => c.trim());
const isSeparator = (cells: string[]) => cells.every((c) => /^:?-+:?$/.test(c));

export function checkDocument(doc: string): Report {
  const report: Report = { passed: 0, failures: [] };
  const expect = (where: string, what: string, actual: string, expected: string) => {
    if (actual === expected) report.passed++;
    else report.failures.push(`${where}: ${what} is printed ${expected}, the engine gives ${actual}`);
  };

  let section = '';
  let header: string[] | null = null;
  let comparison = false;
  const lines = doc.split('\n');
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const line = lines[i];
    const heading = line.match(/^#{1,3} (?:(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\.? |Appendix ([A-Z])\.)/);
    if (heading) section = heading[1] ?? `Appendix ${heading[2]}`;
    const where = section.startsWith('Appendix') ? section : `§${section}`;

    if (!line.trim().startsWith('|')) {
      header = null;
    } else {
      const cells = cellsOf(line);
      if (header === null) {
        header = cells.map(strip);
        // A comparison table names at least one setting; its other columns must all be known.
        comparison = SOURCE_COLUMNS.has(header[0]) && header.slice(1).some((l) => l in SETTING_LABELS);
        if (comparison) {
          for (const label of header.slice(1)) {
            if (!(label in SETTING_LABELS) && label !== 'Jany-Latyn' && !NOTE_COLUMNS.has(label)) {
              report.failures.push(`${where}: comparison column "${label}" is not a known setting (add it to SETTING_LABELS or NOTE_COLUMNS)`);
            }
          }
        }
        continue;
      }
      if (isSeparator(cells)) continue;

      // "Rune | Unicode name" pairs, and Appendix A's code points.
      header.forEach((h, k) => {
        if (h !== 'Unicode name' || k === 0) return;
        const rune = strip(cells[k - 1] ?? '');
        if (!rune || rune === '—' || !RUNE_RUN.test(rune)) return;
        // A cell may hold a pair, "𐰃 / 𐰄" beside "ORKHON I / YENISEI I".
        const names = strip(cells[k]).split(' / ');
        rune.split(' / ').forEach((r, n) => expect(where, `the name of ${r}`, runeName(r) ?? '(none)', names[n] ?? ''));
        if (header![0] === 'Code point') {
          expect(where, `the code point of ${rune}`, `U+${rune.codePointAt(0)!.toString(16).toUpperCase()}`, strip(cells[0]));
        }
      });

      // §2: Jany-Latyn letter → rune.
      if (header[0] === '#' && header[2] === 'Jany-Latyn' && header[3] === 'Rune') {
        expect(where, `the rune for ${cells[2]}`, janyLatynToRunes(strip(cells[2])), strip(cells[3]));
      }

      // Comparison tables: one Cyrillic column, one column per setting.
      if (comparison) {
        const source = strip(cells[0]);
        header.slice(1).forEach((label, k) => {
          const cell = strip(cells[k + 1] ?? '');
          if (label in SETTING_LABELS) expect(where, `${source} in ${label}`, cyrillicToRunes(source, inTables(SETTING_LABELS[label])), cell);
          else if (label === 'Jany-Latyn') expect(where, `${source} in Jany-Latyn`, cyrToJany(source), cell);
        });
      }

      // §14: one row per setting, with the source phrase as a column header in italics.
      if (header[0] === 'Setting') {
        const label = strip(cells[0]);
        const id = SETTING_LABELS[label];
        if (!id) {
          report.failures.push(`${where}: setting row "${label}" is not a known setting`);
        } else {
          header.forEach((h, k) => {
            if (/\p{Script=Cyrillic}/u.test(h)) expect(where, `${h} in ${label}`, cyrillicToRunes(h, inTables(id)), strip(cells[k]));
            if (h === 'Reversible?') {
              const expected = isReversible(presetOptions(id)) ? 'Yes' : 'No';
              expect(where, `whether ${label} is reversible`, expected, strip(cells[k]).startsWith('Yes') ? 'Yes' : 'No');
            }
          });
        }
      }
    }

    // Word examples: *word* (gloss), runes. In tables, only cells of the Example column reach here as text.
    for (const m of line.matchAll(/\*([\p{Script=Cyrillic}][\p{Script=Cyrillic} -]*)\*(?: \([^)]*\))?,? ([\p{Script=Old_Turkic}̇\u{10CEA}]+(?: [\p{Script=Old_Turkic}̇\u{10CEA}]+)*)/gu)) {
      const key = `${m[1]} → ${m[2]}`;
      const id = EXAMPLE_SETTINGS[key] ?? 'jany-enesai';
      expect(where, `*${m[1]}*`, cyrillicToRunes(m[1], presetOptions(id)), m[2]);
    }
  }

  // §4: the passage.
  const passage = doc.match(/> \*\*Cyrillic\.\*\* (.+)\n>\n> \*\*Jany-Latyn\.\*\* (.+)\n>\n> \*\*Jany-Enesai\*\*[^\n]*\n>\n> (.+)/);
  if (!passage) report.failures.push('§4: the passage was not found');
  else {
    expect('§4', 'the passage in Jany-Latyn', cyrToJany(passage[1]), passage[2]);
    expect('§4', 'the passage in Jany-Enesai', cyrillicToRunes(passage[1]), passage[3]);
  }

  for (const e of EXAMPLES) {
    const actual = e.from === 'jany-latyn' ? janyLatynToRunes(e.source, e.options) : cyrillicToRunes(e.source, e.options);
    expect(e.where, e.source, actual, e.runes);
    if (!doc.includes(e.runes)) report.failures.push(`${e.where}: "${e.runes}" (${e.source}) is no longer in the document; remove it from EXAMPLES`);
  }
  return report;
}

function main(argv: string[]): number {
  const path = argv[0] ?? new URL('../../../../docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md', import.meta.url);
  const report = checkDocument(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
  for (const f of report.failures) process.stderr.write(`✗ ${f}\n`);
  process.stdout.write(`Jany-Enesai check (docs/jany-enesai/JANY-ENESAI.md): ${report.passed}/${report.passed + report.failures.length} passed\n`);
  return report.failures.length === 0 ? 0 : 1;
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) process.exit(main(process.argv.slice(2)));
```

- [ ] **Step 9: §27.7, questions returned to Jany-Latyn**

After §27.6 (the paragraph that ends `It is recorded so that no one mistakes the runes for an encoding meant for machines.`), add a blank line and:

```
### 27.7 Questions Returned to Jany-Latyn

Measuring the round trip with the engine (§13) found four places where Jany-Latyn's reverse conversion, or its restoration list, loses Kyrgyz spellings. They are Jany-Latyn's to decide, and the runes inherit whatever it decides. Each is stated with what the treebank shows, not with an answer.

- **Iotated `е` after a vowel** (134 tokens). The reverse rule sends post-vocalic `íe` back as `йе` for the sake of *кийет*. No token in the treebank spells `й` + `е` after a vowel, and every one of the 134 that spell plain `е` is lost: 113 surnames, 10 loans, and 11 native or long-nativized words (§13.1). A corpus with more verbs would show what the rule protects.
- **`и` after a vowel** (23 tokens). The reverse conversion reads `i` after a vowel as `й`, for text that writes the glide as plain `i`. Jany-Latyn writes the glide `í`, so in its own text the rule only loses: *украина* comes back as *украйна*, *Шаирбек* as *Шайрбек*. The question is whether text with a plain-`i` glide still needs reading.
- **`с` before `х`** (1 token). `sh` is read back as the legacy digraph for `ш`, so *схеманы* comes back as *шеманы*. Jany-Latyn writes `ш` as `ş`, so the digraph rule matters only for legacy text; the question is the same.
- **The soft sign in Kyrgyz case forms** (4 word forms). The restoration list gives *апрелге*, *июлга*, *июлда*, and *июлдан* the `ь` of *апрель* and *июль*, which Kyrgyz spelling drops before a Kyrgyz suffix (§13.2). The list could restore the sign only at the end of a word, or only before Russian endings.
```

```ts
// packages/engine/test/specimen.test.ts
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/**
 * The specimen page (scripts/make-specimen.ts): the §4 passage, every preset with
 * its status, and a refusal to render with a font file that is not there.
 */
import { test } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { cyrillicToRunes, RUNE_PRESETS } from '../src/runes/index.js';
import { SPECIMEN_TEXT, specimenHtml } from '../scripts/make-specimen.js';

const golden = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('../../test/fixtures/runes.golden.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8')) as {
  passage: { cyrillic: string };
};

test('specimen: the proposal passage, in every preset, with its status', () => {
  assert.equal(SPECIMEN_TEXT, golden.passage.cyrillic);
  const html = specimenHtml('file:///font.ttf');
  for (const p of RUNE_PRESETS) {
    assert.ok(html.includes(`${p.name} <span>${p.status}</span>`), p.id);
    assert.ok(html.includes(cyrillicToRunes(SPECIMEN_TEXT, p.options)), p.id);
  }
});

test('specimen: a font file that does not exist is refused', () => {
  const script = fileURLToPath(new URL('../scripts/make-specimen.js', import.meta.url));
  const run = spawnSync(process.execPath, [script, '--font', 'file:///no/such/font.ttf'], { encoding: 'utf8' });
  assert.equal(run.status, 2);
  assert.match(run.stderr, /not found/);
});
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Create `packages/engine/scripts/make-specimen.ts`**

```ts
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
/**
 * The specimen of the Jany-Enesai proposal (§4): the passage in every preset, as an
 * HTML page set in the given rune font. Headless Chrome turns it into the PNG the
 * proposal shows (docs/jany-enesai/jany-enesai-specimen.png).
 *
 * Run: node dist/scripts/make-specimen.js --font <font file URL> > specimen.html
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
import { fileURLToPath, pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { cyrToJany } from '../src/convert.js';
import { cyrillicToRunes, RUNE_PRESETS } from '../src/runes/index.js';

export const SPECIMEN_TEXT =
  'Жаңы жылдын биринчи күнү тоого чыгып, бийик чокудан шаарды көрдүк. Үйгө кайтканда чай ичип, эс алдык.';

const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/&/g, '&amp;').replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/"/g, '&quot;');

export function specimenHtml(fontUrl: string): string {
  const rows = RUNE_PRESETS.map((p) => `<h2>${esc(p.name)} <span>${p.status}</span></h2>\n<p class="r" lang="ky-Orkh" dir="rtl">${cyrillicToRunes(SPECIMEN_TEXT, p.options)}</p>`);
  return `<!doctype html>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<style>
@font-face { font-family: "Noto Sans Old Turkic"; src: url("${esc(fontUrl)}"); }
body { margin: 32px 40px; width: 1120px; font: 17px/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif; color: #1f2328; background: #fff; }
h1 { font-size: 20px; margin: 0 0 8px; }
h2 { font-size: 15px; margin: 22px 0 2px; }
h2 span { font-weight: normal; color: #59636e; margin-left: 6px; }
.r { font-family: "Noto Sans Old Turkic"; font-size: 28px; line-height: 1.7; margin: 0; unicode-bidi: isolate; }
.src { margin: 0; color: #59636e; }
</style>
<h1>Jany-Enesai: the passage of §4 in each setting</h1>
<p class="src">${esc(SPECIMEN_TEXT)}</p>
<p class="src">${esc(cyrToJany(SPECIMEN_TEXT))}</p>
${rows.join('\n')}
`;
}

if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  const i = process.argv.indexOf('--font');
  const font = i < 0 ? undefined : process.argv[i + 1];
  // A missing font would not fail the screenshot; the runes would fall back to another font.
  if (!font || (font.startsWith('file:') && !existsSync(fileURLToPath(font)))) {
    process.stderr.write(`usage: make-specimen.js --font <font file URL>${font ? `; not found: ${font}` : ''}\n`);
    process.exit(2);
  }
  process.stdout.write(specimenHtml(font));
}
```

Run: `cd packages/engine && rm -rf dist && npx tsc && node --test dist/test/specimen.test.js`
Expected: `ℹ pass 2`.
